native_result.query: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, how does the number of monuments and axes changes with elements of symbolic capital?
native_result.HypoA: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, the number of monuments and axes increases along with symbolic capital
native_result.HypoB: Between 3400 and 3000 BCE, the relative abundance (Z-score) of monuments (MonumentCount) and axes/celts (AxesCelts) co-varies strongly (r≈+0.87 on the 5 grid points; +0.93 interpolated) and both spike at ~3200 BCE (MonumentCount +0.91, AxesCelts +2.60) before falling back. This monument–axes peak does not track the flat prestige-weapon symbols (HatchetSword≈-0.43; Dagger constant -0.58) but coincides with the steep in-window decline of house size (the one symbolic-capital element that moves), from +2.05 at 3400 BCE to ~0 by 3100–3000 BCE (R²≈0.78). Proposed relationship: as symbolic-capital investment in the domestic domain (house size) declines, monument building and axe/celt prestige-goods production spike — a reallocation of social energy from domestic to monumental/ritual and prestige-goods domains — occurring during declining landscape openness (pollen PC1 MEAN +0.08→-1.86, R²≈0.81) and declining demographic density (kde_all_mean ~-31%; g_all_mean negative throughout), i.e., concentrated symbolic/economic investment despite declining demographic pressure. House size is positively associated with openness (+0.67) and demographic density (+0.95); monuments and axes/celts are negatively associated with demographic density (-0.44/-0.40). Falsified if: the 3200 spike did not coincide with the house-size decline; monuments and axes/celts did not co-move; openness/demographic density were rising during the spike; or the flat weapon symbols spiked instead. All variables are Z-scores (relative abundance, not counts); 5-pt correlations are directional (n=5), 401-pt interpolated correlations are autocorrelated (no significance claimed); the 3200 spike is present in raw observed values; the economic/social-capital labels are the supplied interpretive lens.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded 3 CSVs (time_series_data.csv annual CE -4100..-500; capital.csv 100-yr BCE 4300..500, comma decimals, group=MN in window; pollen file CE -4785..-702, comma decimals). Mapped German capital columns to English names (data-verified by identical 5-pt values). Extracted the inclusive 3400-3000 BCE window (CE -3400..-3000; calBP 4950-5350). Primary analysis on the 5 RAW 100-yr grid points (3400,3300,3200,3100,3000); interpolated/smoothed series used only for trend/correlation sensitivity. Computed: (1) 5-pt window table with core vars + pollen MEAN/SMOOTH_100y + kde/g context; (2) per-variable delta & peak/trough; (3) linear trend slopes & R2 (5-pt primary + 401-pt interpolated); (4) 5-pt Pearson matrix (directional, n=5); (5) 401-pt interpolated Pearson matrix (autocorrelation caveat); (6) openness/demographic trend read. Produced a data-grounded natural-language hypothesis with falsification conditions.
